# Influences and Touchstones

How other works guide this one — at the level of structure, tone, and line-by-line
craft. The negative influences (what we refuse) matter as much as the positive ones.

## Frieren: Beyond Journey's End

> status: ratified (D-0023)

The primary tonal anchor. What we take: emotional sobriety and level-headed competence
(crises met with analysis, not screaming); complete absence of the male gaze
(practical clothing, worth never tied to attractiveness); acoustic, pre-industrial
sound architecture (Celtic-folk textures, the courage to hold silence); the vast,
melancholic anatomy of time (the journey after the quest; grief and memory as
substance); hard logic inside a soft world (magic as a cumulative, academic,
cross-generational science); and narrative archaeology (lore and flashback as the
emotional key to present problems, never exposition filler).

## Inuyasha

> status: ratified (D-0024)

The second pillar. What we take: a center of gravity held by sovereign, competent
female perspectives (the Kikyo/Sango/Kagome trinity of stoic precision, tactical
professionalism, and level-headed adaptation); an acoustic, traditional folk score
oscillating between pastoral peace and mythological dread; the gritty, mud-and-famine
reality of a historical warring era as the sandbox; spirits governed by a strict karmic
taxonomy — ecosystem logic, venoms, nesting habits, structural weaknesses — rather than
generic evil; and a landscape haunted by regret, where the story stops to sit with
unresolved grief.

## Sanderson's "On Fantasy" (2026 Tolkien Lecture)

> status: ratified (D-0025)

The framing contract. This is a true fantasy with allegory undertones — not a pamphlet,
not satire. Sincerity over irony: the characters do not know they are in an allegory;
their physics and terrors are real. We honor Tolkien's process (assemblage of deep
roots into a new subcreation), not his furniture. The piece must deliver the emotion of
exploration — an untamed wild the listener pioneers — plus recovery, escape, and
consolation: hard-won moments of eucatastrophe (the green shoot in poisoned mud), never
cheap despair.

## Austen and the Brontës

> status: ratified (D-0073)

Great stories of women's lives: perfect plots, sharp characterization, strong writerly
voices. The load-bearing influence for [[womens-lives]] and for how conflict plays out
in rooms rather than battlefields.

### The harvest

> status: provisional (D-0073)

How the session mapped it (approved as "a reasonable start"): the violence of
etiquette — confrontations staged as high-stakes, painfully polite negotiations (an
imperial tithe visit played like a drawing-room call from Lady Catherine de Bourgh,
where subtext does the terrorizing); the Brontë gothic — landscape as psychological
mirror, the heroine in painful class liminality (educated above her station, living
below it); Austen's unsentimental economics — survival arithmetic under every polite
surface, the apprentice as the one always running the numbers; and characterization by
contrasting temperament (sense against sensibility against dry, sidelong irony).

## Dune

> status: ratified (D-0027, D-0037, D-0047, D-0068)

Four specific inheritances: growth-of-human-ability as the power system (trained
cognition, not gathered mana); chapter-opening epigraphs from in-world documents (our
narrator's koan cold opens); a deep sense of religious institutions holding real
knowledge across generations (our Wyrd-and-Frith scholar orders); and the
Alia-of-the-later-books condition — a person carrying absorbed other lives, powerful
and costly — as the seed of the protagonist's Archive.

## The manuscript at a remove

> status: ratified (D-0038)

The Handmaid's Tale "Historical Notes" trick (and, more faintly, Tolkien's found
manuscript): this whole story is a record decoded far from the events, by a scholar of
a later era. The remove is the source of the oblique hope — someone survived to study
this.

## Line-by-line touchstones

> status: ratified (D-0082)

Touchstone authors across media guide narration, dialogue, and characterization — not
just plot. Ground rules from the author: keep the Eastern plot structures and the zen
koan parables; avoid immature, stagey anime writing aimed at teens; dark enough for
adults but never Game-of-Thrones trauma exploitation; real wisdom in the narrator,
plausibility in the characters; the protagonist should read as a different sort of
not-quite-human thing, made so by accumulated knowledge and personalities; the whole
serves an ultimately pro-humanistic new flavor of fantasy adventure; songs, poems, and
scraps of ancient history weave in naturally; and the dialogue sounds utterly real and
human.

### Narrator: Le Guin and Susanna Clarke

> status: provisional (D-0083)

Le Guin's spare, mythic, Taoist calm (Earthsea); Clarke's dry, historical
matter-of-factness about magic (Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell). Measured declarative
sentences; no exclamation points; ancient poetry presented as archaeology, not
incantation.

### Dialogue: Tony Gilroy and Hilary Mantel

> status: provisional (D-0083)

Andor's working-class terseness under fascism — rebellion lives in subtext about
stolen parts and shift schedules, never speeches; Wolf Hall's dialogue as polite,
calculating leverage. Nobody monologues a backstory. People talk about the tent, the
wind, the cost — and mean everything else.

### Apprentice: Charles Portis

> status: provisional (D-0083)

Mattie Ross (True Grit): a child in a violent adult world who is never a victim —
stubborn, over-formal, obsessed with exact accounting, relentlessly probing adults for
the rules so as not to be cheated.

### Protagonist's voice

> status: ratified (D-0122)

Her prose model is Ishiguro + Wolfe at the core — Ishiguro's poetic restraint and formal
politeness over oceans of suppressed grief, carrying Wolfe's archaic, elevated density and
his narrator who has absorbed other minds — with Patricia A. McKillip's crystalline lyric
elevation reserved for the high proof-moments and Marilynne Robinson's luminous, plain
humanism for the teaching and pedagogy scenes. Ann Leckie stays rejected as insufficiently
elevated (D-0084); Anne Carson's spare mythic-modern register is excluded as too ironic for
the sincerity mandate (D-0025).

## Tarot and the culture-remapped deck

> status: ratified (D-0147)

A major touchstone of method, beside the narrative touchstones. The tarot tradition —
and above all its culture-remapped descendants (Arthurian, Celtic, witch, and
green-man/wildwood decks) — models the craft this project lives by: take an
archetype grid, map it onto a premodern culture with real scholarship, and dormant
figures wake up as usable characters, settings, and motifs. That is the
hybridization move for this world's cast and places, and it is why the world's own
oracular deck (D-0146) is more than a prop: its figures double as the world's
archetype library, a working tool of the authors' room.
